relevance_note: TMS study describing eight individually tabulated patients with SSADH deficiency (Table 2: "Clinical features of 8patientswithSSADHdeficiency") with per-patient age, neurologic findings, seizures, MRI and medication.
method_note: Tables 1 and 2 were transcribed by a short Python script that slices each patient row; the output was checked against the tables by eye. Labels: the Table 1/2 'Patient' column holds bare numbers 1-8 (with flumazenil-PET study numbers in parentheses, '(no PET)' for patients 5 and 8, ref 14); the table legends use the paper's own label form 'Patients 3 and 4', so all eight are labelled 'Patient <n>' (rule 1) rather than 'Table 1 #<n>'. Relatives: parents whose ages are listed in Table 1 (tested by TMS, called 'obligate heterozygotes' as a group) get rows as 'father of Patient n'/'mother of Patient n'; sex taken from the column header. Table 1 lists '30 (sibling)' in the mother column for Patient 2, recorded as 'sibling of Patient 2' (sex not stated). Patient 4's parent cells are empty (Patients 3 and 4 are sisters); no separate parent rows were made for Patient 4. '-' cells (father of Patient 2, mother of Patient 3) are not described persons and get no rows. Possible inconsistency: Methods state parents numbered 7 male, 6 female (13), while Table 1 lists 6 father ages and 5 mother ages plus one sibling. Variants: no ALDH5A1 variant is printed or tied to any person; diagnosis rests on inclusion criteria (enzyme deficiency or pathogenic mutation, not specified per patient), and parents are only called obligate heterozygotes as a group, so the variants table is empty. Sex: Methods give '4 male' among the patients without naming them; only Patients 3 and 4 ('sisters') get sex. Ages are the Table 1 ages at study (recorded as age at last evaluation). Phenotypes: Table 2 abbreviations expanded using the legend (legend quoted as a second span). Footnote 'All patients had hyporeflexia and motor dyspraxia on examination.' applied to all 8 as a named-group statement; motor dyspraxia mapped to checklist 'gross or fine motor deficits'. Seizures column 'None' recorded as seizures excluded. Absence of an abbreviation from a patient's list is treated as not reported, not excluded. MRI: 'GP, sub, den: bilateral symmetric homogeneous signal abnormalities' recorded as observed features, but the checklist item 'T2 hyperintensity ...' is left not reported because the sequence/direction of the signal abnormality is not stated; Patient 2 'GP volume loss, ex vacuo dilation of the third ventricle' not mapped to 'cerebral or cerebellar atrophy' (focal pallidal volume loss). Patient 8 structural MRI 'Normal' recorded as 'abnormal structural MRI' excluded; per D-27 it excludes nothing more specific, so MRI checklist items stay not reported. Antidepressant/antipsychotic medications (fluoxetine, sertraline, quetiapine, citalopram) were not used to infer depression or psychosis. No stacked cells.
